Since the 1970’s, and increasingly during the last two decades, a slightly different
direction in the study of the statistical behavior of the zeta function has been provided
by a conjectural connection between random matrix theory and the zeta function – for
a brief overview of this connection, see the book review of Conrey [24]. An influential
conjecture in the development of random matrix theory, as well as certain branches of
analytic number theory, has been the Montgomery-Dyson pair correlation conjecture,
which states that after a suitable normalization, the non-trivial zeroes of the zeta
function behave statistically speaking like the eigenvalues of a large random matrix.
